topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices as Dimensional Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Mapping Concept
lecture_lines: A matrix is a mathematical function mapping spaces.
Square matrices map a space into itself.
Non-square matrices bridge spaces of different dimensions.
animations: Create a visual representation of a vector v using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vector.svg].
Draw a transformation T acting on vector v.
Show the resulting transformed vector T(v) using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vector.svg].

sections.title: Case 1: Dimensional Expansion (Tall Matrices)
lecture_lines: Tall matrices have more rows than columns.
They embed lower dimensions into higher ones.
A simple stick figure in 3D space.
animations: Draw a tall matrix mapping R^n to R^m.
Highlight the expansion in dimensions from n to m.
Show vector v moving into the larger space R^m.

sections.title: Case 2: Dimensional Compression (Wide Matrices)
lecture_lines: Wide matrices have more columns than rows.
They compress higher dimensions into lower ones.
This process is called linear projection.
Information is lost during this compression.
animations: Draw a wide matrix mapping R^n to R^m, using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg] to capture the mapping perspective.
Highlight the compression in dimensions from n to m.
Show vector v mapping into the smaller space R^m.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: Tall matrices unfold or embed objects.
Wide matrices flatten or project objects.
Transformation is simply mapping between spaces.
animations: Overlay the tall matrix transformation on screen.
Overlay the wide matrix transformation next to it.
Flash both transformations to summarize the concept.
